land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: Harry Potter and the Escape from Gringotts
kid_note: Both kids will rank it top-3; Bellatrix, Voldemort and the dragon fire can rattle a sensitive 8-year-old.
tip: USF closes at 5 PM on HHN dates, so ride it first at 9 AM; single rider is the fastest backup.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: Hogwarts Express – King's Cross Station
kid_note: Walking through the Platform 9¾ wall is a jaw-drop moment for both kids.
tip: You need a park-to-park ticket. Each direction shows a different story, so ride both ways.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: Ollivanders Experience in Diagon Alley
kid_note: Each show picks one guest for a wand; it's huge if your kid is chosen.
tip: Go in the first hour. Interactive wands work on spell spots all over Diagon Alley.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: Celestina Warbeck and the Banshees
kid_note: Jazzy wizard concert; the 10-year-old will like it more than the 8-year-old.
tip: Use it as a rest stop in Carkitt Market; it alternates on the same stage with Beedle the Bard.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: The Tales of Beedle the Bard
kid_note: Short puppet show of the Three Brothers tale; charming, and it ends before anyone gets bored.
tip: Catch it right before or after Celestina so the two shows run back to back.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: The Knight Bus
kid_note: The wisecracking shrunken head gets big laughs.
tip: It's a walk-up photo op on the London waterfront; check the app for when the conductor is out.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Diagon Alley
name: Death Eaters in Knockturn Alley
kid_note: Masked Death Eaters lurk in the dark alley and may stare down the 8-year-old; the 10-year-old will think it's cool.
tip: Seasonal, Aug 27–Nov 1. Borgin and Burkes is open too.

name: Revenge of the Mummy
kid_note: A 48"+ 10-year-old will love the launches; darkness, fire, scarabs and mummies are too much for most 8-year-olds.
tip: Use single rider or Child Swap. Lockers are required.

name: Race Through New York Starring Jimmy Fallon
kid_note: Silly theater-style race; fun once but not memorable.
tip: The queue gives you a numbered ticket and you wait in a lounge, so the real wait is short.

name: The Blues Brothers Show
kid_note: Kids will likely be bored.
tip: Low priority on a short 9–5 day.

name: ¡Vamos! – Báilalo
kid_note: High-energy Latin dance show; works as a quick stop.
tip: Check the app for times. Treat it as filler.

name: Marilyn & the Diamond Bellas
kid_note: Aimed at adults; kids will shrug.
tip: Skip unless you happen to be passing by.

name: Beat Builders
kid_note: Percussion on buckets and tools; loud fun for kids.
tip: Catch it as you walk between New York and Diagon Alley.

name: MEN IN BLACK Alien Attack
kid_note: Laser-blaster scoring game with spins; kids love beating Dad's score.
tip: Single rider moves fast. Lockers are required.

land: Springfield, U.S.A.: Home of The Simpsons
name: The Simpsons Ride
kid_note: Goofy cartoon chaos, but the dome simulator is rough on queasy kids.
tip: Ride it before lunch, and skip it if anyone gets motion sick.

land: Springfield, U.S.A.: Home of The Simpsons
name: Kang & Kodos' Twirl 'n' Hurl
kid_note: Dumbo-style spinner; fine for an 8-year-old, a 10-year-old will find it babyish.
tip: Only ride if the wait is 10 minutes or less.

land: Springfield, U.S.A.: Home of The Simpsons
name: The Simpsons Character Meet & Greet
kid_note: Quick photo with Homer or Bart.
tip: Check the app for character times.

name: TRANSFORMERS: The Ride-3D
kid_note: The 10-year-old will love the loud 3-D robot battles; the 8-year-old may find the noise and drops intense.
tip: Single rider is often a walk-on.

name: Transformers Meet & Greet (Optimus Prime, Bumblebee, Megatron)
kid_note: Megatron trash-talks you, and kids love it.
tip: Look outside the ride exit.

name: SpongeBob & Friends Meet & Greet
kid_note: Quick photo op.
tip: Check the app for times and location.

name: Despicable Me Minion Mayhem
kid_note: Kids become Minions, and there's a dance party at the end; the simulator bounces more than you'd expect.
tip: Ride in the first or last hour, and ask a Team Member about stationary seating for anyone motion sensitive.

name: Illumination's Villain-Con Minion Blast
kid_note: Video-game blaster on a moving walkway; kids get competitive about scores.
tip: Link the ride to the Universal app to save and compare scores.

name: Illumination Theater (Minions, Gru & the Girls Meet)
kid_note: Hugs with Minions and Gru; the 8-year-old will be the bigger fan.
tip: Check the app for times; lines are usually shorter after 3 PM.

name: E.T. Adventure
kid_note: Gentle bike flight; E.T. saying your name at the end is the payoff.
tip: Give each kid's name at the check-in so E.T. says it at the end.

name: Animal Actors on Location!
kid_note: Dogs, cats and birds doing tricks, with kid volunteers; a sure hit.
tip: Arrive 10 minutes early. Express gets you priority entry.

name: The Bourne Stuntacular
kid_note: The screen-plus-live stunts will amaze the 10-year-old; the gunfire is loud.
tip: Arrive 15 minutes early. It's indoors with AC, so save it for midday heat.

name: Universal Orlando's Horror Make-Up Show
kid_note: Closed during your dates.
tip: Closed for reimagining; reopens Winter 2026.

name: CineSational: A Symphonic Spectacular
kid_note: Won't be running; USF closes at 5 PM for HHN.
tip: Not scheduled for Oct 15–17.

name: Universal Mega Movie Parade
kid_note: Seasonal parade; not running in October.
tip: Ended its summer run Aug 10; TouringPlans lists a Spring 2027 return.

name: Trolls Trollercoaster
kid_note: A perfect first coaster for the 8-year-old; the 10-year-old will want something bigger.
tip: The ride is about a minute long, so skip it if the wait is over 20 minutes.

name: DreamWorks Imagination Celebration
kid_note: Dance-pop show with Shrek, Po and the Trolls; best for younger kids.
tip: A shaded sit-down break; Express gets you priority seating.

name: Po's Kung Fu Training Camp
kid_note: Climbing, gongs and water cannons; both kids will burn energy here.
tip: Reopened July 4, 2026. Bring a spare shirt.

name: Po Live!
kid_note: Closed during your dates.
tip: Closed for refurbishment with no reopening date announced.

name: Poppy's Playground
kid_note: Toddler-skewed; an 8-year-old may get 10 minutes out of it.
tip: Fine for a short break; otherwise skip.

name: Shrek's Swamp for Little Ogres
kid_note: Slides and climbing; good for the 8-year-old.
tip: Pair it with the Shrek meet next door.

name: Mama Luna Feline Fiesta
kid_note: Quick interactive screen game with cats.
tip: Takes 5 minutes; do it in passing.

name: King Harold's Swamp Symphony
kid_note: Musical lily pads you stomp on.
tip: Do it in passing.

name: Shrek, Fiona & Donkey Meet & Greet (Shrek's Swamp)
kid_note: Shrek stays in character and is funny.
tip: Check the app for times.

name: DreamWorks Character Meets (Trolls, Puss in Boots, King Julien, Gabby)
kid_note: Rotating characters; the Trolls are the 8-year-old's best bet.
tip: Check the app for the lineup and times.

name: The Amazing Adventures of Spider-Man
kid_note: Classic 3-D superhero ride; the villains are loud, but the 400-ft 'drop' is an illusion.
tip: Single rider is rarely long. Lines dip mid-afternoon.

name: The Incredible Hulk Coaster
kid_note: Only for a kid who is 54"+ and bold; the launch into the first inversion is intense.
tip: Lockers plus metal detector. Often a walk-on in the first hour or last 30 minutes.

name: Doctor Doom's Fearfall
kid_note: A 185-ft launch tower; 52" rules out most 8-year-olds.
tip: Waits are short all day, so do it whenever you're nearby.

name: Storm Force Accelatron
kid_note: Teacups on steroids; kids control the spin.
tip: Almost always a walk-on. Don't ride after eating.

name: Marvel Character Meet & Greet (Spider-Man, Captain America, X-Men)
kid_note: Spider-Man poses are a hit.
tip: Check the app for times.

name: Dudley Do-Right's Ripsaw Falls
kid_note: The 75-ft drop gives screams and laughs; 44" may rule out the 8-year-old.
tip: You will be drenched. Ride after 1 PM when it's warm and use the paid dryers.

name: Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges
kid_note: The wettest ride in Orlando, and kids think that's hilarious.
tip: Put phones and shoes in the center bin or a locker. Ponchos barely help.

name: Me Ship, The Olive
kid_note: Kids can squirt-cannon the Bilge-Rat riders.
tip: Good while others ride Ripsaw.

name: Toon Lagoon Character Meet (Popeye, Olive Oyl, Betty Boop)
kid_note: Kids likely won't know these characters.
tip: Low priority.

name: Skull Island: Reign of Kong
kid_note: Giant bugs, creepy queue actors and dinosaurs make this one of the scariest rides for an 8-year-old; the Kong finale is currently curtained off.
tip: Running a modified ride since Sept 18 (Kong animatronic damaged). Single rider line removed Sept 2026.

name: Jurassic World VelociCoaster
kid_note: The best coaster in Orlando for a 51"+ 10-year-old; it's off-limits for the 8-year-old.
tip: Do it at Early Park Admission or in the last hour. Lockers plus metal detector; Child Swap available.

name: Jurassic Park River Adventure
kid_note: Closed during your dates.
tip: Closed for major refurbishment; reopens Nov 20, 2026.

name: Pteranodon Flyers
kid_note: Made for the 8-year-old; riders 36–56" only, and anyone taller must ride with a child in that range.
tip: No Express and very low capacity: go first thing or skip it.

name: Camp Jurassic
kid_note: Huge climbing jungle with caves and water spitters; both kids will love it.
tip: Ideal while others ride VelociCoaster. Set a meeting spot, because it's easy to lose kids here.

name: Jurassic Park Discovery Center
kid_note: Watch a raptor 'hatch', see a full T-rex skeleton, play DNA games.
tip: Indoor AC break with no line.

name: Raptor Encounter
kid_note: A realistic raptor up close; thrilling, and slightly scary if it snaps at you.
tip: Runs about 10 AM to 6:45 PM with breaks every 20 minutes. Ask the Team Member how long the line is.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey
kid_note: The castle queue is magical for everyone; the ride has dementors, spiders and lots of swooping motion.
tip: Walk the castle queue even if you don't ride. Lockers required; Child Swap available.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure
kid_note: A 48"+ kid will call it the best ride of the trip.
tip: No Express since July 1, 2026. Rope-drop it at Early Park Admission (8 AM).

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Flight of the Hippogriff
kid_note: Mild family coaster past Hagrid's hut; a confidence-builder for the 8-year-old.
tip: The ride is about a minute long, so use Express or go early.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Hogwarts Express – Hogsmeade Station
kid_note: Different window show from the King's Cross direction.
tip: Needs a park-to-park ticket; lines are usually shorter on the Hogsmeade side.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Ollivanders
kid_note: Same wand-choosing show as Diagon Alley.
tip: Do it in only one park, whichever has the shorter line.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Frog Choir
kid_note: Students singing with giant frogs; short and sweet.
tip: Hourly 11 AM–4:30 PM (late-Sept/early-Oct schedule).

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Triwizard Spirit Rally
kid_note: Durmstrang and Beauxbatons flips and stick-twirling.
tip: Hourly 10:30 AM–4 PM (late-Sept/early-Oct schedule).

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Hogsmeade
name: Dark Arts at Hogwarts Castle
kid_note: Villain projection show on the castle; Voldemort and Death Eaters may spook the 8-year-old.
tip: Runs on select nights Sept 5–Nov 1 after dark, before the 8 PM park close. Confirm Oct 15–17 in the app.

name: The Cat in the Hat
kid_note: Fast spinning couch through the book; the 10-year-old may call it babyish.
tip: Waits are short all day.

name: One Fish, Two Fish, Red Fish, Blue Fish
kid_note: Follow the song's up/down instructions or the squirters get you.
tip: Skip it if the wait is over 10 minutes.

name: Caro-Seuss-el
kid_note: A carousel; the 10-year-old will pass.
tip: Filler only.

name: The High in the Sky Seuss Trolley Train Ride!
kid_note: Slow, scenic elevated train; gentle and cute.
tip: Low capacity: use Express or skip it.

name: If I Ran the Zoo
kid_note: Water-squirting play zone; aimed at younger kids.
tip: Quick cool-off.

name: Oh! The Stories You'll Hear!
kid_note: Seuss characters in a song-and-story show; aimed at younger kids.
tip: Hourly 11 AM–4:45 PM (late-Sept/early-Oct schedule).

name: Seuss Character Meet & Greet (Cat in the Hat, Thing 1 & 2, Grinch, Lorax)
kid_note: Quick photos.
tip: Check the app for times.

name: Stardust Racers
kid_note: A dueling 62-mph racer with big airtime; a 48"+ 10-year-old will want to ride it again.
tip: Lockers plus metal detector. Waits often dip after dark, and the trains glow at night.

name: Constellation Carousel
kid_note: Spinning creature carousel that lifts up to 6 ft; surprisingly fun.
tip: Under 48" needs a companion aged 14+.

name: Astronomica
kid_note: Splash pad with geysers; kids will get soaked on purpose.
tip: Bring a change of clothes. Good while others ride Stardust.

name: Universal Celestial Goodnight
kid_note: Fountains, lights and fireworks paying tribute to Mario, Berk, Potter and the Monsters; a great finale.
tip: 8:00 PM at park close on Oct 15–17. Stake out the amphitheater around the Cosmos Fountain 20–30 minutes early.

name: Captain Cacao Meet & Greet
kid_note: Quirky space-explorer character; quick photo.
tip: Between Pizza Moon and The Oak & Star Tavern; added May 2026.

name: Mario Kart: Bowser's Challenge
kid_note: A dream for Mario fans: you throw shells in AR goggles and race Team Bowser, and the castle queue is epic.
tip: Go first at Early Park Admission or use Express. Single rider is also an option.

name: Mine-Cart Madness
kid_note: Carts appear to 'jump' track gaps; both kids will love it.
tip: Longest wait in the park. Use Express, single rider, or be first in line at Early Park Admission.

name: Yoshi's Adventure
kid_note: Slow egg hunt on a Yoshi; the 10-year-old may find it slow.
tip: Use Express or ride late. It has the best overhead views of the land.

name: Bowser Jr. Challenge
kid_note: A boss battle you play by punching keys; big win for kids with Power-Up Bands.
tip: Requires a Power-Up Band (purchase); collect keys from land-wide mini-games first.

name: Mario & Luigi Meet & Greet
kid_note: Must-do photo for Mario fans.
tip: Lines are shortest in the first hour or the late afternoon.

name: Princess Peach Meet & Greet
kid_note: Gazebo by the castle.
tip: Check the app for times.

name: Toad Meet & Greet
kid_note: Quick, fun photo.
tip: Center of Mushroom Kingdom.

name: Donkey Kong Meet & Greet
kid_note: The big DK costume impresses kids.
tip: At the Donkey Kong Country treehouse; pair it with Mine-Cart Madness.

name: Monsters Unchained: The Frankenstein Experiment
kid_note: Genuinely frightening robot-arm ride (Dracula, Wolf Man, jump scares); only for a brave 48"+ 10-year-old.
tip: Waits are usually short. Lockers required; Child Swap available.

name: Curse of the Werewolf
kid_note: Spinning family coaster with a dark werewolf shed; fun, but spin-prone kids may get sick.
tip: Low capacity, so use Express or single rider.

name: Dark Universe Character Encounters
kid_note: Roaming Frankenstein's Monster, Bride and Invisible Man interact in character; could spook the 8-year-old.
tip: Walk-up encounters around Darkmoor village.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Ministry of Magic
name: Harry Potter and the Battle at the Ministry
kid_note: The Floo Network intro and Umbridge trial wow both kids; the 40" minimum means the 8-year-old can go.
tip: Go first at Early Park Admission or use Express. Single rider is the backup.

land: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Ministry of Magic
name: Le Cirque Arcanus
kid_note: Fantastic Beasts circus with acrobats and huge puppets; a hit with both kids.
tip: About 12 shows a day, 10:30 AM–7:10 PM. Line up 20 minutes early or use Express.

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: Hiccup's Wing Gliders
kid_note: Smooth launched family coaster with Toothless; the best 'big' coaster an 8-year-old can ride.
tip: Lockers required (or a small fanny pack). Ride in the first hour or with Express.

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: Dragon Racer's Rally
kid_note: Riders tilt their own wings to flip and barrel-roll; a 48"+ 10-year-old will love it.
tip: No Express and very low capacity, so go at park open or the last hour. Covered cubbies on board.

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: Fyre Drill
kid_note: Viking boat water-cannon battle; both kids will love blasting each other.
tip: Covered chests on board for bags. Waits are often 15 minutes or less.

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: Viking Training Camp
kid_note: Shaded climbing towers, slides and rope bridges; the 8-year-old will love it.
tip: Best wait-spot while others ride Dragon Racer's Rally.

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: The Untrainable Dragon
kid_note: Live musical with a full-size flying Toothless; a top pick for the kids.
tip: About 11 shows a day, 11:10 AM–7 PM. Arrive 15–20 minutes early or use Express.

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: Meet Toothless & Friends
kid_note: A lifelike Toothless that moves and reacts; unforgettable for dragon fans.
tip: The line is long all day, so get in it right at open or in the last hour (Haddock Paddock).

land: How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk
name: Berk Character Encounters (Astrid & Stormfly, Gobber, Ruffnut & Tuffnut, baby dragons)
kid_note: Baby dragon puppets are a kid favorite.
tip: Walk-up; check the app for times.
